newsitem.title: CYPRUS: AIDS sufferer finishes evidence in Cyprus trial.
newsitem.headline: AIDS sufferer finishes evidence in Cyprus trial.

text.p: A three-day court ordeal for British AIDS sufferer Janette Pink ended on Saturday as she left a Cypriot judge to decide whether her former Cypriot lover was guilty of knowingly giving her the killer virus.

"I would just like to say the court handled my evidence with great compassion and I am glad that I finished giving my evidence," a relieved-looking Pink, 45, told reporters in the sunny yard of a court in the coastal town of Larnaca.
"I am just looking forward now to going back home to be with my family and to get on with my life."

Pink, from Basildon, Essex, has accused former boyfriend Pavlos Georgiou, 40, of giving her the virus, a charge he denies. She reported Georgiou to the authorities last year when she returned to Britain to seek medical treatment.
She tested HIV positive in October 1994, nine months after her affair with Georgiou, a local fisherman and builder, started.

Now the woman, painfully thin, is on around 30 tablets a day and has just a few years to live. Georgiou, a burly man with four children, is HIV positive but shows no apparent signs that he is suffering from any illness.

"I don't make long term plans, obviously," she said when asked whether she would be returning to Cyprus. "With my health situation I don't know how long I am going to have left to live but I am going to make the most of it with my family."
Pink refused to speak to Georgiou outside the courtroom when his identical twin brother Petros approached her.
In statements to reporters Petros accused a member of Pink's family of trying to make money out of the affair, and the media of being biased against his family.
"I believe...responsibility lies with both of them, from the knowledge and experience I have of this whole story, and I think that the two are guilty, and innocent," he said.

Earlier, Pink remained composed under persistent questioning by defence counsel, insisting that Georgiou concealed from her that he was HIV positive, telling her his AIDS-stricken wife Martha was dying of leukaemia.
"I never had any reason to suspect anything other than her dying of leukaemia," Pink told the court.
Pink dismissed repeated submissions from Georgiou's defence lawyer Tassos Economou that his client always used a condom, saying he never did so.
In an earlier court appearance Pink said she went for tests after Georgiou's mother-in-law told her her daughter died of AIDS.

Georgiou has been charged that through negligence he committed an act that could transmit a life-threatening disease. The charge carries a prison sentence of up to two years, a 1,500 pound fine, or both.
